items.title: Jury sides with OpenAI, rejects Musk's lawsuit

featured_image.name: Jury Sides With OpenAI, Sam Altman in Case Brought by Elon Musk - WSJ

items.description: A federal jury in Oakland, California, sided with OpenAI and Sam Altman on Monday, rejecting Elon Musk's lawsuit alleging the artificial intelligence company betrayed its nonprofit mission when it shifted toward a for-profit model. The nine-member jury found that Musk's case was filed too late, ending the closely watched legal battle that had threatened to upend one of the most valuable private companies in the world.

items.title: Pakistan sends 8,000 troops, jets to Saudi Arabia

featured_image.name: Pakistan sends fighter jets to Saudi Arabia under defence pact - TRT World

items.description: Pakistan has deployed approximately 8,000 troops, a squadron of around 16 JF-17 fighter jets, two drone squadrons, and a Chinese-made HQ-9 air defense system to Saudi Arabia under a confidential mutual defense agreement, Reuters exclusively reported on Sunday. The deployment, described by five sources as a "combat-capable force," marks the largest Pakistani military commitment to the Gulf kingdom since the 1991 war against Iraq and comes even as Islamabad serves as the principal mediator in the ongoing Iran war.[1][2]

items.title: Iran launches Strait of Hormuz transit authority as US reinsurance program draws zero takers

featured_image.name: Iran officially announces new body to manage Strait of Hormuz: top security  council - The Economic Times

items.description: The Trump administration's flagship effort to restart commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a $40 billion government-backed reinsurance program — has failed to attract a single customer, according to industry reports and insurer statements, even as Iran moves to assert sovereign control over the waterway with its own transit authority and a cryptocurrency-backed insurance scheme.

items.title: U.S. offers temporary Iran oil sanctions waiver in new draft text

featured_image.name: Trump administration moves to cut off Iranian oil exports

items.description: The United States has offered to temporarily waive sanctions on Iranian oil exports during active negotiations, according to Iran's Tasnim News Agency, marking a potential shift in Washington's approach to ending the nearly three-month war. But the proposal has done little to break the diplomatic deadlock, with Iran demanding full and permanent sanctions removal and President Trump warning Tehran on Sunday that "the clock is ticking."

items.title: Pakistan shares revised Iran peace proposal with US amid stalled talks

featured_image.name: Revised Iranian proposal to end war shared with US, Pakistani ...

items.description:
Pakistan shared a revised Iranian proposal with the United States on Sunday night aimed at ending the conflict in the Middle East, a Pakistani source told Reuters on Monday, even as peace talks appeared to remain stalled.[1][2]

"We don't have much time," the source said when asked whether it would take time to close gaps between the two sides, adding that both countries "keep changing their goalposts".[1]

items.title: Man charged with murder after woman and two children found dead in Sydney home
items.description: A man, 47, has been charged after three people were found dead in a home in Sydney's south-west in what police allege is a domestic violence-related incident.

items.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts three drones from Iraqi airspace

featured_image.name: Saudi Arabia intercepts over 60 drones amid rising Iran–US tensions

items.description:
Saudi Arabia said on Sunday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed three drones after they entered the kingdom's territory from Iraqi airspace, marking the latest in a series of aerial threats that have tested Gulf security since the broader Iran conflict erupted earlier this year.

Defense Ministry spokesman Major General Turki Al-Maliki said the kingdom "would take the necessary operational measures to respond to any attempt to violate its sovereignty and security" and vowed to ensure the safety of citizens and residents on Saudi territory, according to Arab News.[1]

items.title: Taiwan's Lai vows island 'will not be sacrificed' after Trump-Xi summit

featured_image.name: Taiwan-US ties are 'rock solid,' the island's president says after Trump-Xi  call

items.description:
Taiwan President Lai Ching-te on Sunday pushed back against the suggestion that the island's security could be used as leverage in U.S.-China diplomacy, declaring that "Taiwan will absolutely not be sacrificed or traded" and that its people will not surrender their democratic way of life under pressure.[1][2]

Writing on Facebook in his first direct response to last week's summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, Lai reaffirmed that U.S. arms sales to Taiwan are rooted in the Taiwan Relations Act, the 1979 law that mandates weapons sales to the island, and called them "the most important deterrent force over the years against actions that undermine regional peace and stability".[2][1]

items.title: Trump warns Iran 'the clock is ticking' as strike preparations intensify

featured_image.name: Trump to speak with Netanyahu as military action on Iran ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his rhetoric toward Iran on Sunday, posting warnings on Truth Social that "the Clock is Ticking" and threatening that there "won't be anything left" of Iran if it does not agree to American terms, as the United States and Israel advanced preparations for a potential resumption of military strikes and a drone attack struck near a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates.

The warnings came as Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a phone call on Sunday. Netanyahu said earlier in the day, "Our eyes are also open regarding Iran. I will speak today, as I do every few days, with our friend President Trump. There are certainly many possibilities, and we are prepared for every scenario."[1]

items.title: WHO declares Congo-Uganda Ebola outbreak a global health emergency

featured_image.name: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda a public ...

items.description:
The World Health Organization on Sunday declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern, its highest level of alarm, after more than 300 suspected cases and 88 deaths were reported across the two countries.[1][2]

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus made the declaration after consulting with both governments, warning of "significant uncertainties to the true number of infected persons and geographic spread" of the disease. The agency said the outbreak is "potentially much larger than what is currently being detected and reported, with significant local and regional risk of spread".[3][4][1]

items.title: Iranian drone strike sparks fire at UAE's Barakah nuclear plant

featured_image.name: Barakah, first nuclear power plant in UAE, starts commercial operations

items.description: A drone strike attributed to Iran caused a fire at an electrical generator on the outer perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Abu Dhabi's Al Dhafra region on Sunday, according to Abu Dhabi authorities and reports from Al Jazeera and Gulf News. No injuries were reported, and officials said radiological safety at the facility was not compromised.[1][2]
